text:
Incident Bot: [pager] High 429 spike for customer AtlasHealth (dedicated-pool-42) — alerts at 1951234567. Impact: approx 23% of requests returning 429s, 100% of realtime routes on pool-42. Pager routed to oncall.
Anita Kaur: paging, seeing a spike in 429s from AtlasHealth dedicated pool 42. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/metrics/pool/42 spike at 1951234500.
Lee Park: ACK. pulling logs now. can you post the tenant id and any recent deploys?
Anita Kaur: tenant atlashealth-nyc, no recent model deploys from them. last infra deploy was 1951231200 (autoscaler tweak).
Matt Simmons: I see autoscaler logs show rapid scale-in earlier today, then a burst of queued requests. possible burst rate gating hit.
Jen Morales: Support is on thread. Jen -> contacting AtlasHealth SRE to notify them we're investigating. Eli, FYI for contract/overrides.
Eli Navarro: On it. looping in sales/legal if we need a temporary contract override for emergency burst. what's the immediate mitigation?
Lee Park: Two quick mitigations: 1) emergency rate-lift for atlashealth tenant to bypass soft quota for 30m, 2) route their high-throughput realtime model to a fallback instance group or model-variant with higher concurrency.
Anita Kaur: Agreed. starting emergency lift runbook. tagging @deploy-bot to run the lift script.
deploy-bot: Command received: `/run emergency-rate-lift --tenant atlashealth-nyc --pool 42 --duration 30m --reason "unexpected 429 spike"`
deploy-bot: Executing: updating tenant rate override, updating routing policy. Logs: 
```
2026-03-14T18:22:54Z INFO rate-override applied tenant=atlashealth-nyc duration=30m requested_by=anita
2026-03-14T18:22:55Z INFO routing-rule applied tenant=atlashealth-nyc target_variant=gptx-rl-fallback-quant
```
Matt Simmons: I pushed a temporary routing change: atlashealth realtime -> gptx-rl-fallback-quant (reduced latency but lower cost). Watch for regressions.
Jen Morales: AtlasHealth SRE confirmed they see lower 429s now and are re-running failed requests. They asked about tokenization differences — passing to model ops to validate output parity.
Lee Park: Metrics look better: 429s dropped from 23% -> 2% within 90s of lift. https://redwood.internal/alerts/1951234567/graph screenshot attached.
Anita Kaur: Good. recording timeline in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1951234567. Action: follow up on autoscaler tweak that precipitated this.
Eli Navarro: For contract/temporary credit: propose we absorb emergency lift for this weekend; follow-up with PM to scope if billable. I'll draft a note to acct.
Matt Simmons: Root cause hypothesis: aggressive scale-in policy + bursty client retry pattern. Need a mitigation in autoscaler: minimum healthy nodes for enterprise pools or smoothing window for dedicated tenants.
Ryan Cho: I'm taking over oncall at 1951235600 — will monitor for the next 4 hours. Anita/Lee, leave any runbook notes here for handoff.
Anita Kaur: Thanks Ryan. Handoff notes: emergency lift applied, routing to fallback variant, metrics link + logs in incident doc, pending tasks: revert routing after traffic normalizes and run canary for model parity.
Lee Park: Open tasks created: INF-7892 (increase min nodes for pool-42), SRE-3421 (analyze client retry pattern), OPS-1200 (add smoothing to autoscaler).
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: `/revert emergency-rate-lift --tenant atlashealth-nyc --at 1951237367` (automated revert in 30m).
Ryan Cho: I'll watch the revert and confirm with AtlasHealth before revert. If 429s return, we'll extend and coordinate dedicated capacity bump.
Jen Morales: Sent post-incident note to AtlasHealth support channel and offered a callback with our infra leads tomorrow.
Incident Bot: Incident status: mitigated -> degraded->monitoring. Incident closed for page at 1951235999, follow-up tasks assigned.
